title: Enforcement Decree of the Special Act on the Commemoration and Subsequent Use of the Yeosu World Expo
title_original: 여수세계박람회 기념 및 사후활용에 관한 특별법 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Special Act on the Commemoration and Subsequent Use of the Yeosu World Expo and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Expo Facilities)
"Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Special Act on the Commemoration and Subsequent Use of the Yeosu World Expo (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following facilities:
1. Facilities developed to host the Expo, such as the International Pavilion, Sky Tower, and aquarium;
2. Facilities, such as accommodation facilities and commercial facilities, newly developed in accordance with the plan for the subsequent use of Expo facilities under Article 14(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "subsequent use plan").

Article 3 (Businesses Relating to Subsequent Use of the Expo)
"Businesses prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4(2)3(c) of the Act means the following businesses: <Amended 2023.5.2>
1. Exhibitions using Expo facilities and sites, and businesses incidental thereto;
2. Businesses of leasing facilities and sites owned by the Yeosu Gwangyang Port Authority established pursuant to Article 4(2) of the Port Authority Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Yeosu Gwangyang Port Authority").

Article 4
Deleted. <2023.5.2>

Article 5

Article 6 (Subsidies)
To receive support under Article 5 of the Act, the Yeosu Gwangyang Port Authority shall submit an application for a subsidy to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, accompanied by a business plan and a budget execution plan. <Amended 2023.5.2>

Article 11 (Criteria, etc. for Formulation of Subsequent Use Plans)
When formulating a subsequent use plan pursuant to Article 14(1) of the Act, the Yeosu Gwangyang Port Authority shall take the following matters into consideration:
1. Consistency with relevant urban plans, such as the urban master plan of Yeosu City;
2. Carrying on and commemorating the spirit and achievements of the 2012 Yeosu World Expo;
3. Efficient means of financing, such as attracting private investment;
4. Links between the project area covered by the subsequent use plan (hereinafter referred to as the "target area") and surrounding areas.

Article 11-2 (Affairs and Composition, etc. of the Expo Subsequent Use Committee)
(1) Pursuant to Article 14(2) of the Act, the Expo Subsequent Use Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established under the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to deliberate on the following matters related to subsequent use of the Expo:
1. Matters concerning the formulation of subsequent use plans;
2. Other matters that the chairperson of the Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "chairperson") deems necessary in relation to subsequent use of the Expo.
(2) The Committee shall consist of no more than 15 members, including the chairperson, with consideration given to gender.
(3) The Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall serve as the chairperson, and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall appoint or commission members from among persons falling under any of the following subparagraphs. In such cases, the members shall include at least five persons who are residents of the city having jurisdiction over the Special Marine Expo Zone (hereinafter referred to as the "special zone") and are among the persons referred to in subparagraphs 2 and 3.
1. One person each designated by the head of the relevant institution from among public officials belonging to the Senior Civil Service or Grade III public officials of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and of the Do and city having jurisdiction over the special zone;
2. Persons with extensive expertise and experience in land use, urban planning, architecture, landscapes, or the like;
3. Persons with extensive expertise and experience in the 2012 Yeosu World Expo, marine leisure and tourism, marine culture, marine and fisheries industries, coastal development, the marine environment, or the like.
(4) The term of office of members under paragraph (3)2 and 3 shall be two years.
(5) The Committee may have one secretary to handle its affairs, and the secretary shall be designated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries from among public officials belonging to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 11-3 (Operation of the Committee)
(1) The chairperson shall represent the Committee and oversee all of its affairs.
(2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform the duties of office for an unavoidable reason, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on the chairperson's behalf.
(3) The chairperson shall convene and preside over meetings of the Committee.
(4) A meeting of the Committee shall open with the attendance of a majority of the incumbent members and adopt resolutions by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(5) Where necessary to deliberate on the matters referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 11-2(1), the Committee may hear the opinions of interested parties or experts in relevant fields.
(6) Members attending meetings of the Committee may be paid allowances and travel expenses within budgetary limits. Provided, That this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends in direct connection with the duties under that member's jurisdiction.
(7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters necessary for the operation of the Committee shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 11-4 (Public Notice of Subsequent Use Plans)
When publicly notifying a subsequent use plan in the Official Gazette pursuant to Article 14(3) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall include the following matters:
1. The basic direction of the subsequent use plan;
2. The location and area of the target area;
3. The land use plan within the target area;
4. Measures for linking the target area with surrounding areas.

Article 12 (Amendment of Subsequent Use Plans)
"Changes to minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 14(4) of the Act means any of the following changes: <Amended 2023.5.2>
1. A change of less than 10 percent in the area of the target area;
2. A change to land use plans, etc. affecting an area smaller than 10 percent of the target area;
3. Changes in the locations and structures of Expo facilities due to circumstances such as topography or physical space.

Article 13 (Hearing of Residents' Opinions, etc.)
(1) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries intends to hear the opinions of the Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction and of residents on the designation or amendment of the designation of a special zone pursuant to the main clause of Article 15(2) of the Act, the Minister shall send the relevant documents to the Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction, and the Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction may submit their opinions to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries if they have opinions on the contents of the relevant documents received. <Amended 2023.5.2>
(2) The Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction who have received the relevant documents pursuant to paragraph (1) shall, without delay, publicly announce the principal details of the designation or amendment of the designation of the special zone in at least two daily newspapers whose main circulation area is the whole country or the relevant Do or city and on the websites of the relevant Do and city, and shall make the documents available for inspection by residents within their jurisdiction for at least 14 days.
(3) A person who has an opinion on matters publicly announced pursuant to paragraph (2) may submit the opinion in writing or by electronic means to the Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction during the inspection period under paragraph (2). <Amended 2023.5.2>
(4) The Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction shall submit the written opinions submitted pursuant to paragraph (3) and their written review opinions on those opinions to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within seven days from the date on which the inspection period ends; where no opinions have been submitted, they shall inform the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries of that fact.
(5) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall inform the Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction of the results of processing the written opinions and written review opinions submitted pursuant to paragraphs (3) and (4), and the Do Governor and mayor having jurisdiction shall inform the persons who submitted opinions pursuant to paragraph (3) of the results of processing those opinions.

Article 14 (Changes to Minor Matters Concerning the Designation of Special Zones)
The term "where minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree are changed" in the proviso to Article 15(2) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where the area of a special zone is changed by less than 10/100 of its area;
2. Where land use plans, etc. are changed with respect to less than 10/100 of the area of a special zone.

Article 15 (Public Notice of the Designation of Special Zones)
When publicly notifying the relevant documents in the Official Gazette pursuant to the former part of Article 15(3) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall include the following matters:
1. The purpose of the designation of or change to the special zone;
2. The location and area of the special zone;
3. The land use plan;
4. The topographical map under Article 8(2) of the Framework Act on the Regulation of Land Use.

Article 16 (Restrictions on Activities, Etc.)
(1) The term "activities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 16(1) of the Act means cutting or planting bamboo or trees.
(2) The term "activities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 16(2) of the Act means the following activities: <Amended on January 5, 2021; January 10, 2023>
1. Construction of buildings: Construction, major repair, or change of use of buildings under Article 2(1)2 of the Building Act (including temporary buildings);
2. Installation of structures: Installation of artificially constructed facilities (excluding buildings under Article 2(1)2 of the Building Act);
3. Alteration of the form and quality of land: Changing the form of land by methods such as cutting (cutting away earth), filling (piling up earth), leveling (leveling the ground), or paving (surfacing), excavation of land, and reclamation of public waters;
4. Collection of earth and stones: Collecting earth and stones, such as soil, sand, gravel, and rocks: Provided, That collection for the purpose of altering the form and quality of land shall be governed by subparagraph 3;
5. Capture or collection of aquatic animals and plants, or aquaculture: Fishing access under subparagraph 8 of Article 2 of the Fisheries Act, recreational fishing (fishing for recreation) under subparagraph 17 of that Article, and aquaculture under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act;
6. Subdivision of land.

Article 17 (Implementers of Projects for the Subsequent Use of Expo Facilities)
The term "private investors meeting the qualification requirements, such as those concerning capital, prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 3 of Article 17 of the Act means any of the following persons: <Amended on October 30, 2018>
1. A person registered to engage in a business category undertaking general construction works under the Framework Act on the Construction Industry, whose assessed construction capacity value, publicly disclosed pursuant to Article 23 of that Act, is at least the average annual project cost (excluding compensation costs) of the relevant project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities;
2. A trust business entity under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act that is subject to external audit under Article 4 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc.;
3. A person owning at least 50/100 of the land area within the area in which the relevant project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities is implemented (hereinafter referred to as the "project implementation area");
4. A public-private joint corporation under subparagraph 12 of Article 2 of the Act on Public-Private Partnerships in Infrastructure;
5. A real estate trust company holding in trust at least one-third of the land area of the project implementation area;
6. A corporation (including a corporation scheduled to be established; hereinafter the same shall apply) that finances at least 10/100 of the total cost of the relevant project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities (hereinafter referred to as the "total project cost") with equity capital. In such cases, where the corporation has multiple capital contributors, the sum of the contribution ratios of the three capital contributors with the highest contribution ratios shall exceed 50/100.

Article 18 (Approval of Implementation Plans, Etc.)
(1) Where a person implementing a project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities (hereinafter referred to as a "project implementer") intends to obtain approval for the project implementation plan pursuant to Article 18(1) of the Act, the project implementer shall submit to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries an application for approval of an implementation plan for a project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities in the attached Form, accompanied by an implementation plan that includes the following matters: Provided, That the matters specified in subparagraphs 2, 3, 7, and 9 shall be included only where applicable.
1. A location map of the project implementation area;
2. The location, lot number, land category, and area of the land, objects, and rights to be expropriated or used (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc."), details of ownership and rights other than ownership, and the names and addresses of their owners and rights holders;
3. Plans for the purchase of and compensation for land, etc., and measures for the relocation of residents;
4. Layout plans and schematic design documents;
5. The project implementation period;
6. A financing plan;
7. Plans for the relocation and removal of public facilities and for the installation of replacement facilities;
8. An environmental impact assessment report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act;
9. A damage impact survey report based on a survey conducted by a specialized research institute or educational institution in fisheries designated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries;
10. Documents necessary for consultation with the heads of relevant administrative agencies under Article 19(3) of the Act.
(2) Upon receipt of an application for approval under paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall check the cadastral map of the area in which the project is to be implemented through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act.
(3) When deciding whether to approve an implementation plan under paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall consider the following matters:
1. Whether the contents of the implementation plan are consistent with the plan for the project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities;
2. The appropriateness of the plans for the purchase of and compensation for land, etc., and the measures for the relocation of residents;
3. Whether the contents of the layout plans and schematic design documents comply with the relevant statutes and regulations;
4. The appropriateness of the financing plan.
(4) The term "where minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree are changed" in the proviso to Article 18(1) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on June 15, 2015>
1. Where the area of the project implementation area is changed by no more than 10/100 of its area;
2. Where the total project cost is changed by no more than 10/100 of that cost;
3. Where the period of the relevant project for the subsequent use of Expo facilities is changed by no more than 1 year;
4. Where the location and structure of equipment or facilities are changed;
5. Where the name or address of the project implementer (where the project implementer is a corporation, meaning its name, location, or the name of its representative) is changed;
6. Where errors or omissions are corrected.
(5) Where any matter in an implementation plan falling under any subparagraph of paragraph (4) is changed, the project implementer shall notify the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries of the details of the change without delay. <Added on June 15, 2015>
